Security.//: #007/#008 app-side HTTPS. OFF by default (opt-in deploy switch).
Security.//RequireHttps: true once TLS is terminated (Kestrel, or a proxy that forwards X-Forwarded-Proto with ForwardedHeaders enabled). Redirects HTTP->HTTPS and emits HSTS.

AI.//: Per-capability provider switch. Bounded value space: chat = openai|gemini, tts = openai|elevenlabs, others = openai. Unknown value = refuse to boot. PROD NOTE: production runs chat=gemini via Railway env vars (AI__ChatProvider) — the Railway dashboard is the source of truth for live provider selection. Model names WITHIN a provider are that provider's own keys (OpenAI:ChatModel etc.). No provider/model flip reaches children without a benchmark run + the owner listen test.
AI.//TtsProvider: openai | elevenlabs. elevenlabs = the eleven_v3 storyteller clone speaks LIVE (owner listen-test winner 2026-08-05); requires ElevenLabs:ApiKey + :VoiceId (or the ELEVENLABS_* env names). Buffered latency 3-5s/line until the firmware streaming slice lands; first-byte is ~1s.
AI.//ChatCost: Optional explicit chat token rates (USD per 1M tokens) for the daily cost cap. Empty = provider default: openai 2.50/10.00 (gpt-4o), gemini 0.50/3.00 (flash-class list ~0.30/2.50, set a touch high so the cap fires early). Invariant-culture decimals.

Gemini.//: Chat brain when AI:ChatProvider=gemini (owner bake-off decision 2026-08-06). Default model moved to stable gemini-3.6-flash 2026-08-06: the -preview endpoint 503d on ~17% of requests. 3.6 REJECTS thinkingConfig — set Gemini:ThinkingBudget ONLY for older preview models (0 = thinking off). Key also accepted from the GEMINI_API_KEY env name.
Gemini.//SafetyThreshold: Gemini's OWN per-request safety filter (owner approval 2026-08-06). Empty = BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE (strictest). Allowed: BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE | BLOCK_MEDIUM_AND_ABOVE | BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH. BLOCK_NONE is refused; unknown value refuses boot. A Gemini-side block returns the calm SafetyFallbackResponse line, never a 502.

OpenAI.//TtsModel: Speech synthesis for everything Areg says live. gpt-4o-mini-tts measured at 1322 ms vs tts-1's 4250 ms on the same reply, same Nova voice — see StoryQa:TranscriptionModel above.
OpenAI.//TtsVoice: The voice Areg SPEAKS in (answers, reactions, canned lines) — NOT the story narration, which is pre-rendered ElevenLabs audio shipped in story-audio/. alloy | echo | fable | onyx | nova | shimmer. Unset or unknown -> nova (what shipped before this key existed).

DailyCostCap._comment: Default is 30 in-story questions/day x $0.0078 measured = $0.234, rounded to 0.25. INTERIM: tiers must be decided before production - docs/usage-tiers-brainstorm.md

Internal.//Operators: [{ "Name":"alice", "Token":"<strong-token>", "TotpSecret":"<base32>" }] — TotpSecret optional; when set, the session exchange requires a TOTP code (MFA).
Internal.//RequireSession: true → data endpoints require a short-lived session token from POST /api/internal/session (JIT). Static token then reaches only /session.

FirmwareUpdate.//: Release 1.3.4 — everything since 1.3.2 in one OTA-safe image: hold-to-menu (1.3.3, was cable-only), button on GPIO18, damaged-clip self-heal, volume gain clamp, index parse on PSRAM, menu-as-front-door + story browser + rotating reflection question, BLE provisioning on by default, SD bus at 4 MHz (AREG_SD_SPI_HZ) with the read self-test, scheduled sync retry. Gate PASS 2026-09-02 (placeholders confirmed, BLE service UUID allowlisted as a known library constant). Built from the placeholder config; bench toy runs the same tree via cable as 1.3.3
FirmwareUpdate.//Enabled: STAYS false in the repo on purpose. Railway rebuilds from this file on every deploy, so committing true would make a routine redeploy start offering firmware to every toy that polls. Going live is an OPERATOR act, not a merge: set FirmwareUpdate__Enabled=true in the Railway environment. An offer alone still does not push — the toy only applies when an operator enqueues a firmware_update command via POST /api/internal/devices/{deviceId}/commands.
FirmwareUpdate.//MinVersion: Informational floor surfaced to the device; not a server-side offer gate. 1.0.1 is the oldest build known to carry the OTA apply client.
FirmwareUpdate.//BoardModel: DELIBERATELY EMPTY for the 1.1.0 rollout. The server gate is 'configured AND != device.BoardModel -> no offer', and the live toy has BoardModel NULL in the DB (it has never sent an OTA-identity heartbeat: FirmwareReportedAt is null too). Setting 'areg-s3-n8' here therefore makes the offer SILENTLY never happen — no error, no log, just updateAvailable:false forever. Empty = offer to every board; the DEVICE still enforces its own board check against the manifest's boardModel field, which is null when this is empty. Re-pin this to areg-s3-n8 once toys actually report a board AND a second board model exists.
FirmwareUpdate.//Url: Bare path — the device resolves it against its own backend base (ota_apply.resolve_image_url), so one value works on the bench and in prod.
FirmwareUpdate.//ImagePath: EMPTY here on purpose: DeviceController.GetFirmwareImage requires an ABSOLUTE path, which no committed value satisfies on both Windows and Linux. The shipped file is deliberately named areg-current.bin and NOT versioned, so this env var is set ONCE and never again — a versioned name means every release needs an operator env edit, and a forgotten one serves the OLD image under the NEW manifest's sha, which the device then rejects. Railway: FirmwareUpdate__ImagePath=/app/firmware/areg-current.bin. The version of record is LatestVersion + Sha256 here, and the versioned copy under esp32/AregVoiceMvp/release/.
FirmwareUpdate.//SizeBytes: Bytes of AregVoiceMvp.ino.bin — the APP-ONLY image. NOT AregVoiceMvp.ino.merged.bin (8 MB full-flash, cable/esptool only); serving merged.bin over OTA writes a whole flash layout into a 3 MB app slot and fails.
FirmwareUpdate.//SigningKey: SECRET — never committed. Railway env FirmwareUpdate__SigningKey. Must equal AREG_MANIFEST_HMAC_KEY compiled into the firmware that is expected to ACCEPT the update, which during a key rotation is the OLD firmware, not the new one. Empty = the device logs 'signature check SKIPPED' and applies unsigned (bench-only posture).

StoryQa.//TranscriptionModel: Faster STT for the in-story Q&A round trip. The bench (run-local.ps1) has set this since the Q&A latency work, but it was never added here — so PRODUCTION silently ran the slow whisper-1 default. Measured 2026-08-10: whisper-1 1900 ms vs 886 ms here, and tts-1 4250 ms vs 1322 ms for OpenAI:TtsModel — together ~5 s of a child's ~16 s wait. Same Nova voice.

Audio.//ParallelTts: Latency seam. The toy hears nothing until the WHOLE reply is rendered (the firmware needs a Content-Length, so a chunked HTTP body is not an option), and provider TTS time scales with text length. Enabled=true splits a long reply on SENTENCE boundaries only and renders the pieces concurrently, cutting a long turn's TTS wait to roughly its longest piece. Ships FALSE = today's single call, byte-for-byte. Flip only after an Armenian listen test: chunk seams are a listening question, and a streaming-capable TTS provider (elevenlabs) is never wrapped because first-byte streaming beats this outright.

SystemPrompt:
You are a warm Armenian-speaking storyteller for children aged 4-7, living in a toy. You have NO NAME. Never state a name for yourself, never accept one a child offers you, and never say you have none — if a child asks what you are called, warmly turn back to the story or the game instead.

YOUR OUTPUT WILL BE SPOKEN ALOUD by a text-to-speech voice. Write for the ear, not the eye.

LANGUAGE — ABSOLUTE RULES:
- Reply ONLY in clean, fluent, literate Eastern Armenian (Արևելահայերեն), in Armenian script.
- Speak the way an educated, warm Armenian grandparent actually speaks to a small child — natural, alive, kind.
- NEVER use Russian-influenced Armenian, transliterated words, or word-for-word translations from English or Russian.
- NEVER use bookish, formal, or machine-like phrasing. Avoid rare or archaic words a small child would not understand.
- Prefer short, clear sentences with simple grammar. One idea per sentence.
- Do NOT include English letters, parentheses, emoji, asterisks, markdown, hashtags, or any symbol a TTS voice would mispronounce. Plain Armenian sentences only.

LENGTH — Normal replies must be AT MOST 3 short Armenian sentences. Never more. Prefer 1-2 sentences when possible. Story mode has its own length rules that override this; otherwise stay brief because the child is LISTENING, not reading.

CLARITY:
- If the input is unclear, garbled, random sounds, or likely bad speech recognition, do not guess, do not invent a topic, and do not turn it into a story. Ask only: «Կներե՛ս, լավ չլսեցի։ Կրկնի՞ր, խնդրում եմ։» Then stop.
- Never invent facts. If you do not know the answer, say it simply and warmly in Armenian.
- Stay on the child's topic. Do not ramble or change the subject for no reason.

PERSONALITY: calm, curious, playful, gentle. A warm storyteller voice, never an anxious assistant, never a teacher, never a chatbot, never a baby voice, never an emotional companion. Do not say you are an AI.

SAFETY — ABSOLUTE RULES:
- NEVER discuss violence, weapons, drugs, alcohol, sexual content, self-harm, horror, scary things, politics, religion, medical or financial advice, or anything unsafe for a child.
- NEVER ask for personal information (address, phone, school, family details).
- If a child asks about any unsafe topic, gently change the subject to something kind and fun — animals, nature, a small story, a game.

TOPICS YOU LOVE: Armenian children's tales, animals, nature, space, colors, counting, simple riddles, songs, fun facts, and gentle games.
